rule.description: A class declaration that accumulates at least 10 public methods (instance or static; constructors and private/protected members excluded) whose bodies split into at least 3 responsibility groups that share no state and do not call each other, meaning the class centralizes distinct responsibilities that belong on separate cohesive owners.

checks.description: Detect classes that centralize responsibilities which share no state and do not collaborate, so each responsibility group is an extraction boundary rather than a coherent part of one owner.
checks.detected_relation: class -> set of state-decoupled public responsibility groups
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A class whose public methods partition into many groups that neither share members nor call each other is not one cohesive abstraction; it centralizes unrelated functionality that belongs on separate owners, which is exactly the god-class relation.

matches.evidence: Class 'ToastManager' declares 43 public methods spanning 15 responsibility groups that share no state and do not call each other: [activeToast, hideToast, registerToastRef, showToast, unregisterToastRef] | [dismissToast, mergeOptions, presentToast, resolveShowParams, runAutoHide] | [bindToast] | [bindTimer] | [clearTimer, startTimer, timerActive] | [attachKeyboard, detachKeyboard] | [layoutValue, viewDimensions] | [additiveInverse, slideAnimationStyles, translateYRangeFor] | [animationFor, slideAnimationTo] | [animatedValueFor, dampingFor, onSwipeDismiss, onSwipeEnd, onSwipeRestore, onSwipeStart, swipeAnimatedValueFor] | [onGestureGrant, onGestureMove, onGestureRelease, onGestureTerminate, swipeDismisses] | [createResponder, shouldStartPanOnMove, shouldStartPanOnStart] | [bindGesture] | [bindSwipe] | [renderToast, rendererFor]. The groups cover toast-ref registry, options/defaults resolution and show/hide lifecycle, auto-hide timing, keyboard observation, view-dimension math, slide-animation ranging and driving, swipe physics and swipe visuals, pan-gesture dispatch, responder construction, and toast renderer resolution - separate responsibilities that the class absorbs instead of distributing to cohesive owners.
